claims.text: Between February and June 2025 the owner wrote five essays on diniscruz.ai that took the Portugal talks to the scale of Europe.
claims.quote: Five essays, February to June 2025.

claims.text: The Europe and learning hub holds the five essays, each with a PDF: on Portuguese as a programming language, a sovereign cloud, regulation as graphs, Europe's opportunity in GenAI, and the EU federated cloud compared.
claims.quote: The Europe and learning hub on diniscruz.ai holds them, each with a PDF

claims.text: If natural language is the new programming language, then Portuguese, spoken by more than 260 million people on four continents, needs models, tools and data of its own, built in the open with the government involved.
claims.quote: spoken by more than 260 million people on four continents, needs models, tools and data of its own

claims.text: Digital sovereignty is not just about infrastructure; it is also about language and culture.
claims.quote: it is also about language and culture

claims.text: Portugal released Amália, an open-source model for European Portuguese built on EuroLLM and funded through the national recovery plan, as a platform for public services; the other varieties are still waiting.
claims.quote: built on the European EuroLLM and funded through the national recovery plan, as a platform for public services

claims.text: The sovereign cloud proposal: a European cloud that is 100% open source, fully compatible with the major cloud APIs so nothing has to be rewritten, and federated so countries, regions and cities run their own parts.
claims.quote: full compatibility with major cloud APIs

claims.text: The June essay compared it with the EU's federated cloud initiative, an alliance of providers with a jointly designed service, against the Linux of cloud that anyone can host or modify.
claims.quote: the 'Linux of cloud' that anyone can host or modify

claims.text: In June 2025 Microsoft France's legal director, asked by the French Senate whether he could guarantee French data would never reach US authorities without consent, said he could not guarantee it.
claims.quote: asked whether he could guarantee French data would never reach US authorities without consent

claims.text: The answer is no longer one new cloud but to move the cloud, not the code: keep the code portable, keep the server dumb and hold the keys yourself, so that sovereignty is the ability to move.
claims.quote: keep the code portable, keep the server dumb, and hold the keys yourself, so that sovereignty is the ability to move

claims.text: sgit is built that way: the server holds ciphertext, and whoever holds the keys holds the line.
claims.quote: sgit is built that way: the server holds ciphertext

claims.text: Europe's regulatory superpower has a weakness: NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act and the AI Act are published as flat documents, the same for everyone.
claims.quote: are published as flat documents, the same for everyone

claims.text: Turn the regulations into semantic graphs so a company can ask what applies to it, in its context, with every answer linked to the article it came from.
claims.quote: so a company can ask what applies to it, in its context, with every answer linked to the article it came from

claims.text: This became the owner's work: fractal semantic graphs, the books on graphs.sgit.ai and a regulation graph of the AI Act with 1,523 nodes all descend from it, and every article on this site carries a graph.
claims.quote: a regulation graph of the AI Act with 1,523 nodes

value.unit: nodes in the AI Act regulation graph

claims.text: The regulation got more urgent: the Cyber Resilience Act's reporting duties started on 11 September 2026 and the new product liability rules start in December.
claims.quote: the Cyber Resilience Act's reporting duties started on 11 September 2026, and the new product liability rules start in December

claims.text: The fourth essay named six trends that play to Europe's strengths: commoditised deterministic models with provenance, AI at the edge, knowledge as semantic graphs, multilingual AI, open source and decentralisation, and a human-centred vision.
claims.quote: commoditised models and deterministic AI, with provenance; AI moving from the cloud to the edge; knowledge moving from text to semantic graphs

claims.text: The direction held more for some trends than others: the edge moved less than expected and the cloud models more, since most of the owner's agent work runs on large models in the cloud.
claims.quote: The edge moved less than I expected, and the cloud models moved more

claims.text: For the new Hacking Portugal the essays are the wider frame: the lever is no longer only security or code, but language, graphs and the ability to move.
claims.quote: the lever is no longer only security or code, but language, graphs and the ability to move

claims.text: A year and a half later two of the essays have moved, Amália and graphs, and the sovereign cloud has not yet.
claims.quote: Amália and graphs, yes; the sovereign cloud, not yet.

claims.text: Not that the essays caused Amália: many people asked for a Portuguese model.
claims.quote: Many people asked for a Portuguese model.

claims.text: The sovereign cloud is not dead: the owner thinks there is a better route, not that it is wrong.
claims.quote: I think there is a better route, not that it is wrong.

claims.text: The commentary is the owner's, now; the essays are from 2025, unchanged.
claims.quote: The essays are from 2025, unchanged.

claims.text: The Microsoft France exchange at the French Senate comes via The Register, a translation reported second-hand.
claims.quote: via The Register, a translation reported second-hand
